changes: Image attachments (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP, TIFF) are now scanned with on-device OCR (tesseract.js, vendored under extension/vendor/tesseract/) — screenshots and photos of documents are read in the browser and any SSNs, emails, or other PII they contain trip the same per-piece verdicts as typed text. Nothing is uploaded; OCR runs entirely inside the sandbox iframe

Archive attachments (.zip, .tar, .gz/.tgz) are now expanded and each contained file is scanned individually — a bundle.zip shows one row per inner file (e.g. 'bundle.zip → q2/payroll.csv'). Nested documents, spreadsheets, slide decks, and images inside the archive are extracted and OCR'd too

Zip-bomb / fork-bomb protection: archive expansion is bounded by entry count, total uncompressed size, per-entry size, and nesting depth; anything past the limits is surfaced as a 'review manually' row instead of being processed
Encrypted or unsupported archive types (.7z, .rar, password-protected) fall back to 'review manually' rather than being silently passed through
Larger files are now scanned: per-file cap raised to 25 MB, combined attachment cap to 100 MB, up to 32 attachments per send, and up to 200 KB of extracted text per file

Excel (.xlsx) attachments are now scanned end-to-end — the sandbox iframe parses the workbook itself and pulls text from xl/sharedStrings.xml plus every xl/worksheets/sheet*.xml so SSNs, emails, and other PII inside spreadsheet cells trip the same per-piece 'What we scanned' verdicts as a CSV
DEFLATE-compressed XLSX entries are decompressed in-browser via DecompressionStream('deflate-raw') (Chrome ≥80) — no extra vendored library shipped
If the file is not a real .xlsx (legacy .xls binary, password-protected, malformed) the row falls back to 'couldn't read the spreadsheet — review manually' instead of being silently passed through
Per-file 5 MB / combined 15 MB / 50 KB-extracted-text caps continue to apply unchanged

PDF text extraction now uses pdf.js (vendored under extension/vendor/pdfjs/), so the firewall reads CMap-encoded fonts, hex strings, TJ kern arrays, and other real-world PDF shapes — not just hand-laid-out content streams
Word (.docx) text extraction now uses mammoth (vendored under extension/vendor/mammoth/), covering more complex documents than the previous minimal ZIP/XML walker
Sandbox replies now travel over a private MessageChannel transferred per request, so extracted text never lands on the host page's window message bus
PDF and Word (.docx) attachments are now read inside the browser and analyzed alongside the prompt — no more 'review manually — content not scanned' rows for those file types in the common case
Extraction runs inside a sandboxed iframe (manifest.sandbox.pages → src/sandbox.html) over a postMessage RPC, so the parsing code lives in its own opaque-origin context separate from the host AI page
If the sandbox can't be reached or the file can't be parsed (encrypted PDF, image-only scan, malformed docx) the row is still surfaced as a 'review manually' skip, never silently passed through
Per-file 5 MB / combined 15 MB / 50 KB-extracted-text caps continue to apply; nothing changed about the burst-rate or analyze-port plumbing

Firewall now scans file attachments (txt, csv, tsv, json, md, log, xml, html, yaml, ini, sql) before they leave your browser — the Send/Enter trigger is unchanged, but anything you've attached to the composer is read and analyzed alongside your prompt
Per-file results are listed in the warning panel so you can see exactly which file tripped which rule; the worst result across prompt + files determines the overall verdict

PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), images, and archives are detected by type and explicitly flagged 'review manually — content not scanned in this version' rather than being silently let through. You always have to make an explicit Cancel / Send Anyway choice when an unscannable file is attached
Per-file 5 MB cap, combined 15 MB cap; oversize files are surfaced with the same 'review manually' treatment so a 200 MB log can't crash the page or quietly slip past the firewall
Sanitize button is hidden when the only blocker is a file (it would only rewrite the prompt, leaving the file in place)

Hard 15-second client-side timeout on the analyze flow — the firewall overlay can no longer get stuck on 'Analyzing your prompt…' if the background service worker is suspended mid-fetch. After the timeout the user always sees a clear error panel with recovery actions

Error panel is now visually unmistakable from the analyzing panel: red-orange header accent, alert icon, and 'Couldn't analyze' headline copy — at a glance during a demo you know which state you're in

Error panel adds a third 'Open Extension Popup' button alongside Close and Send Anyway, taking the user straight to the API key + connection status (with a clipboard-copy fallback hint if the browser blocks the auto-open)
Popup shows a new 'Last attempt' line under the connection card (success / failed / no response — Xs ago) so you can self-check mid-call whether the previous prompt actually hit the API

Firewall now ALWAYS shows a result panel — clean prompts get a brief 'All clear' confirmation that auto-sends after ~1.2s but exposes Cancel during the window. Removes the silent auto-bypass that previously dismissed the overlay and clicked Send with no feedback

Detector now catches casually-typed sensitive content: short fake-key strings (sk-fake1234, Bearer abcd, ghp_short), contextual passwords/PINs/account numbers, partial/space-separated SSNs, dates of birth, residential addresses, credit card numbers without separators, and disclosed full names
Any single detected issue now caps the risk score below the 'safe' threshold so the warning panel always renders when something was found
Simplified API config — the firewall now talks only to https://eraseai.ai. Removed the optional Custom API URL field, the apiUrl storage key, and the related recovery flow
Tightened host permissions to just the AI chat sites the content script runs on, plus eraseai.ai for the API

New public, no-login status page at https://eraseai.ai/status with live API health, latest extension version, last-checked timestamp, and a one-click 'Copy install link' button — usable on sales and support calls
Production builds now only accept eraseai.ai (and *.eraseai.ai) as the API host; *.replit.app is reserved for development builds
Popup explains clearly when a custom API URL is rejected on a production build
Stored custom URLs that fall outside the allowlist are silently ignored and the firewall falls back to eraseai.ai
Self-diagnosing popup distinguishes server-unreachable, missing key, and invalid key with one-click recovery
Reset API URL action restores the default eraseai.ai endpoint when a custom URL is misconfigured
Get-my-API-key shortcut always opens the canonical eraseai.ai dashboard, bypassing any wrong custom URL
/api/dev/ping is now a public health probe, returning the user's plan when called with a valid API key
Added support for Gemini and Claude prompt interception
Improved overlay rendering performance on long prompts
Tightened host permissions to *.eraseai.ai and *.replit.app
Fixed popup not saving custom API URL on Edge
Resolved race condition when sanitizing very short prompts
Initial release of the EraseAI Firewall extension
Risk analysis, sanitize, and send-anyway flows for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Replit
